name: Shephatiah
overview: Shephatiah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Reuel according to 1 Chronicles 9:8. There are no additional notes or significant details about his life beyond this familial connection. His mention in Scripture is brief, focusing primarily on his lineage within the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Shephatiah means "y-h-v-h has judged," reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's judgment. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:8, was not given directly by God but carries the significance of divine judgment as part of its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Shephatiah was the son of Reuel, as stated in 1 Chronicles 9:8. It is also inferred that Meshullam was his father, indicating a generational link within his family line. Beyond these relationships, the biblical record does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Shephatiah's significance in the biblical narrative lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Benjamin. His identification as the son of Reuel helps establish the continuity of the Benjaminite lineage, which is important for understanding the tribal structure and heritage of Israel. Though not a prominent figure in terms of actions or leadership, his mention contributes to the faithful recording of God's people as preserved in Scripture.
